payload.entry: NOTE FROM sase-1tc.3.1.land: the TASK RESOLVED: sase-1c2 evidence in note #2 came from a harness that faked chop-agent records as cl_name=<agent name>. Production records use the project name or VCS ref, and the recovery code matches on that field, so spawn-before-ack reconciliation does not work in production. Child-epic remaining work under sase-1tc.3.1 fixes this and will record superseding TASK RESOLVED evidence here. Do not treat sase-1c2 as resolved until then.

DISCOVERED ISSUE: efc66a420b (sase-1tc.1.1.2) makes #research name the PRIMARY research checkout, so reports land outside the commit finalizer's scan and are silently never committed. Cause: macro bodies now run their own $(...) during expansion (src/sase/macro/_processor_render.py:123). The runner expands macros (run_agent_runner_bootstrap.py:442) before it enters the workspace (:448). With no workspace marker in cwd, `sase repo path research --ensure` (sase-research-artifacts xprompts/research.md:39) falls back to workspace #0 (repo_handler_common.py:87-89). Before efc66, $(...) ran at the provider call inside the workspace. Impact on apollo: 0 of 96 #research runs Nov 15 to Nov 17 14:28 named the primary path; all 24 from Nov 17 15:30 did (sase, bob-cli, tailnet). Of those, 7 committed (the agent wrote into a checkout it had opened) and 11 finished with no research commit. Concrete case: agent ex (run 20261118095611) opened research at its workspace clone, but wrote 202611/overnight_backlog_epic_chains_audit.md to the primary checkout. The clone stayed clean, so final context was not_triggered / submission_required=false and the commit finalizer reported success with empty evidence. The file is still untracked in the primary. Suggested fix: resolve launch-time macro commands inside the claimed workspace, or pass the runner's workspace number to `sase repo path`. A finalize-time check for untracked writes outside scanned repos would also have caught it (see related sase-1g1). Report: research:202611/research_report_finalized_without_commit.md (file:explicit:6c500d0b78ec209c6a77680b).

payload.entry: DISCOVERED ISSUE: sase-1tj.1 note #1 proposes resolving the general launch-time cwd hazard caused by efc66a420b (sase-1tc.1.1.2). Landing review at fbfaf07123 confirms _processor_render.py executes eligible macro-body commands while run_agent_runner_bootstrap.py calls preprocess_prompt_macros before enter_agent_workspace; repo_handler_common.resolve_list_workspace_num returns workspace 0 without a matching marker. Research-specific macros are fixed in plugin 73b3350, but other authored cwd-sensitive commands still see the launch cwd. Please evaluate entering an already-known workspace before expansion or preserving source provenance while deferring execution until after claim, including deferred launches. Routed here via /sase_new_task; same causal issue as note #2, not a duplicate task or a request to weaken the cmdsub trust model.

TASK RESOLVED: sase-1c2 — production-shaped chop batch recovery re-proved end to end. This supersedes note #2 here, which rested on fakes with an impossible cl_name evidence shape. Harness now uses real chop-agent linkage records written from launch env (cl_name=sase project name), the real name registry, explicit pipe/file handshakes, an isolated SASE state root, a disposable job and harmless short-lived processes. 17 subprocess scenarios green on ordinary AND typed paths: k-of-n k=0/2/4; SIGKILL after spawn-before-ack (dismissed agent) and after reservation-before-spawn; SIGTERM finishing the current launch; second restart launches zero everywhere; routine/manual race (loser blocked live-owner, no duplicate, exactly one interrupted+resumed); clan kill while paused, while recovery-active (crossing member settles, rest never start), and typed equivalents; multi-clan batch (unrelated clan and stale generation leave it alone; either clan cancels); two interruption episodes (exactly 2 interrupted + 2 resumed, 2 delivered episodes in the archived outbox, including a resume prepared by a killed recovery). Asserted per scenario: n distinct original identities, exactly n spawns, resumed linkage points at the original run+proposal index, original run history lists all n launches once, original clan/run identity, termination mode, notices+log lines. Acceptance fixes landed in this phase: (1) run history now merges pre-interruption launches backfilled from durable linkage (ordinary) plus resumed+reconstructed rows (typed), so history lists every member exactly once; (2) typed resume replays lost spawn acknowledgements for linkage-proven dispatching units instead of skipping them; (3) finish notices emit before executor release+retire, so a racing recovery cannot duplicate an episode notice or orphan the outbox. Typed first runs finalize their launched rows; typed proposals carry clan identity; fake spawns the planner-namespaced member identity. No Rust/binding changes, sase-core pin untouched. Verification: 17/17 acceptance green; focused suites green (batch recovery/replay/store 57, clan-launch/lifecycle/once-per/typed-admission/runner/inflight/tick 59+48+6); sase tool run check run a070819049c2e7ea8a5669652cb2ff29 STATE succeeded EXIT 0 (all lint incl. mypy+symvision, scoped lane 135 files). Disposable demo repeated via python -m tests.axe.chop_batch_process_harness demo: stop/resume 1 spawned then 3 remaining then 0, interrupted+resumed notices with 1-launched-3-remaining / 4-launched-0-remaining log lines; clan kill retained cancelled with cancelled notice.
